description:
## Goal

Resolve each callable name exactly once at its legitimate source boundary, then retain the typed FunctionId through quote, macro execution, unquote, expansion, and lowering. Source spelling and qualified names exist only before resolution and for diagnostics or macro-visible display.

## Correct model

A call target is either unresolved source syntax paired with its exact lexical owner, or an already-resolved FunctionId. Once resolved, no later phase may stringify, qualify, parse, look up, reconstruct, or globally search for that identity. Literal code inside quote retains its definition binding; unquoted caller code retains its caller binding; dynamically constructed quoted source enters the ordinary resolver once.

Keep the standard quoted AST shape. Encode the typed target in the call node existing metadata: missing target metadata means fresh unresolved syntax; Bound(FunctionId) is authoritative even if a macro changes the visible head spelling. Creating a new semantic target requires fresh unresolved metadata, not a display-string edit. Argument changes validate the bound arity and never choose another overload by spelling.

World remains the one identity and namespace authority. The owning QuotedSourceHeap carries one shared World identity-domain token inherited by roots and subroots; it does not retain World. Bind the heap when compiler-owned identities first enter it, preserve or validate the domain during cross-heap transport, and reject malformed or foreign bound identities before probing World. Do not serialize World identity into every node or introduce a resource, side table, namespace snapshot, fallback resolver, or parallel binding store.

## TDD signal

Use the cross-source macro case exposed during fz-tfn.53: App binds FutureMacros only as F, requires F.twice/1, and the provider macro quotes a call to its own double/1 helper. Prove both separate submission orders, driving only after the provider exists: each returns 42 and lowers the helper call to the exact provider FunctionId. fz-tfn.46 owns the earlier requester-drive boundary, where today's unknown-import failure must become an observed exact ModuleInterface dependency and resume only when that provider arrives.

Also prove a caller binding the spelling FutureMacros to a different module cannot redirect the quoted helper; and an unquoted caller-local reference retains caller scope while the quoted helper retains definition scope. Assert identities with lowered/function captures, not rendered names.

Prove copied metadata and head-only edits preserve a bound target; fresh metadata creates unresolved syntax at the assigned owner; argument edits cannot retarget overloads; malformed, out-of-range, and foreign-World targets diagnose without panic; and typed targets survive interpreter/native tuple-map transport. Preserve macro inspection/composition, semantic equality, deterministic unchanged/unrelated zero work, and byte-identical artifacts.

## Strategy and deletion

Delete quoted_callable_name and every canonical module.function string used as post-resolution authority. Delete downstream generated-call module-path re-resolution and any workaround that adds provider names to caller namespaces or globally falls back from failed lexical lookup. Collapse quote and ordinary call lowering onto one typed call-target path; keep spelling and span only for diagnostics and macro-visible syntax.

Update quoted-source and macro-expansion documentation to state the single-resolution invariant and metadata contract. Full focused/library/fixture/CLI gates, formatting, check, strict Clippy, and a fresh ticket-scoped cold adversarial review precede one commit and close. No compatibility path or construction debris remains.
title: Keep callable identity through quoted source; delete canonical-name re-resolution
